newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp reports modest gain in interim profit.
newsitem.headline: Sharp reports modest gain in interim profit.

text.p: Japanese electronics maker Sharp Corp. Thursday reported a slim gain in its half-year profits but said economic uncertainty had cast a cloud over its outlook for the rest of the year.
Sharp said its current profit rose 3.1 percent on a parent company basis to 36.11 billion yen ($319 million) in the six months to September, the first half of the business year ending next March 31.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities such as investment in stocks.

The low yen and acquisitions of low-cost parts and materials in overseas markets helped the business in the first half, Sharp said in a statement. Earnings were helped by a strong rise in sales of audio and communications equipment.

Analysts said a good showing in household appliances also helped offset slower sales of electronic components, which include Sharp's mainstay businesses such as liquid crystal display (LCD) computer panels and flash memory chips.
A delay in the start-up of a new LCD plant in the Kansai area of western Japan affected its LCD sales, said Kazuya Yamamoto, analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research.
Sharp said sales of electronic components inched down 1.3 percent compared with the same period last year, while those of audio and communications equipment rose 20.1 percent.
Sharp said severe business conditions are likely to continue in the second half of the business year, citing uncertainties over exchange rates and interest rates.

It trimmed its parent current profit forecast for the full 1996-97 year to 74 billion yen ($654 million) from the 77 billion yen ($681 million) forecast it made in late May. The revised figure would be an increase of around five percent from the profits in the previous fiscal year.
